objective: Preregister and batch-screen 15 candidates (12 primary LETF_{SPY,QQQ,SMH}_D{2,3}_H{1,3} leveraged-ETF close-rebalancing-flow-reversal candidates plus 3 internal RAND placebo controls) for T-20260929-01 part A (gap-search 2026-09-29-01, flows_structural.rebalance_and_hedging_flows; registry dir:letf_close_rebalancing_flow_reversal, queued) via scripts/screen_batch.py --batch h20260929_01_letf_flow_reversal --iteration h20260929_01_letf_flow_reversal against the owner's K1/K2 keep rule. No return, Sharpe or backtest number is computed in this dossier.
target_regime_and_horizon: Same frozen windows as every batch-screening round in this repo: stress 2016-05-02..2023-09-15 and anchor 2024-01-08..2026-09-17, judged on date-neutral Sharpe. D frequency, one version per candidate (no rebalance-day offset sweep, per screen_lane.py's docstring -- this is an event-driven daily rule, not a calendar-anchor with a shiftable rebalance day). The 2026-01-02..2026-09-17 holdout is reference-only and contaminated. Validity is limited to the local SIP daily archive's coverage for SPY/QQQ/SMH/SHY (2016-01-04 onward) -- no new data fetch is needed. This mechanism is mechanical (daily leverage-ratio rebalancing), not behavioral, so a priori it should not have decayed the way calendar anomalies have -- but Lenkey (2024)'s own synthesis reads the class-level economic magnitude as small, so the recent-regime bar this batch applies (K1/K2 vs S3) is a real test, not a formality.
existing_solution_comparison: `oc research directions check letf` and `check dip` (run this session, transcript below) found: dir:letf_close_rebalancing_flow_reversal itself is 'queued' (this task's own registry entry, added by the same 2026-09-29 gap search that produced this queue task -- a match against itself, not a prior distinct test); dir:etf_dip_reversion_ibs_connors is 'refuted' (a different RSI(2)/IBS dip signal, re-judged here under a different keep bar by the companion h20260929_01_dip_rejudge iteration, not this one); dir:option_expiration_week_calendar_effect is 'refuted' (a different, calendar-anchored dealer-hedging-flow mechanism, same K1/K2 contract, 0/8 primary). No prior local iteration tests a same-ticker magnitude-conditioned drop-then-reversal rule on SPY/QQQ/SMH. This is the first local test of this specific mechanism. Lenkey (2024) is the one genuinely new source opened for this round (by the coordinator, in the queue task; not re-fetched in this execution session -- see external-brief.json's reflection field); its own literature review already synthesizes the underlying LETF-flow papers (Ivanov & Lenkey, Cheng & Madhavan, a 2022 SFI working paper), so a second independent read of those was judged low-value given the survey's synthesis already states the class-level conclusion this batch tests locally.
remaining_evidence_gap: Whether any of the 12 primary lookback-free event-driven candidates actually clears K1, K2, strong_keep or watch_recent against S3's frozen reference numbers when run through the batch-screening lane under this project's 10bp/20bp next-open-fill cost contract, and whether any apparent edge survives the same-ticker RAND placebo falsification -- this is exactly what has not been tested locally and is what this round's screening pass computes, with no further parameter choice available to it once the manifest is frozen.
negative_experiments_checked: h20260928_42_opex_week (another mechanical dealer/hedging-flow mechanism under the identical K1/K2 contract: 0/8 primary refuted, all negative anchor Sharpe, corroborated by an internal placebo) and h20260924_01_etf_dip_reversion (0/24 at the older G1/G1' bar, D1's own placebo failure) both set the recent-round base rate: published flow/reversal mechanisms have repeatedly failed this project's specific contract even where the underlying academic mechanism is judged real by its own source. Lenkey (2024)'s own synthesis already reads the LETF-rebalancing-flow literature as economically insignificant despite statistically significant individual-paper associations -- this batch is a direct, cheap test of whether that holds locally, not an assumption that it does.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: 10bp per side primary, 20bp per side stress, signal at the session close, fill at the next session's open (both entry and exit) -- identical to the frozen S1/S2/S3 convention and every prior batch-screening round (cost-contract.json). Retrigger-while-holding is ignored (no extend, no stacking) -- a fixed, preregistered convention documented in candidate-manifest.json, not a choice made after seeing any result.
stop_condition: If none of the 12 primary candidates clears K1, K2, or reaches watch_recent (or every apparent pass is beaten by its own same-ticker RAND placebo), dir:letf_close_rebalancing_flow_reversal is refuted for this scope and the flows_structural.rebalance_and_hedging_flows gap-search entry is closed for this specific mechanism; the next round should not re-tune this same threshold/hold grid on this same universe without a new, distinct signal (e.g. an actual AUM/flow-magnitude proxy from options or fund-flow data this repo's data does not yet support).

queries.query: Lenkey 2024 leveraged ETF market impact survey AIMSPress Quantitative Finance and Economics (curl fetch + WebFetch re-verification, this execution session)

sources.claim: Survey of the leveraged/inverse-ETF rebalancing-flow literature (Lenkey 2024, AIMSPress Quantitative Finance and Economics, open access). The literature consistently reports statistically significant associations between ETF rebalancing demand and late-day returns and volatility, but most papers suffer potentially serious methodological errors and the economic associations appear insignificant; concerns raised by policymakers are not supported by the overall empirical evidence.
sources.market_and_period: US leveraged/inverse equity-index ETFs, literature survey (no single sample period -- synthesizes multiple studies)
sources.applicability: Sole mechanism grounding for all 12 LETF_* primary candidates and the honest prior that the economic effect is likely small.
sources.limitations: A survey, not a single dataset with its own Sharpe/return figures to replicate directly; the underlying papers it reviews were not independently opened this round.
sources.independent_replication: n/a -- this batch's own local screen is the decisive test.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Run all 15 candidates through the batch-screening lane (scripts/screen_batch.py --batch h20260929_01_letf_flow_reversal --iteration h20260929_01_letf_flow_reversal) against S3's frozen stress/anchor windows and check K1/K2/placebo-falsification directly; the engine and cost/fill convention are already frozen and reused unedited, so this is the cheapest possible resolution.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: At least one of the 12 primary candidates clears K1 or K2 in candidate-manifest.json's keep_rule AND is not demoted by the RAND placebo internal falsification rule.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: None of the 12 primary candidates has a date-neutral Sharpe >=80% of S3's in both windows with positive 20bp CAGR (K1), none of their 63-session inverse-vol blends with S3 beats a vol-matched k*S3+(1-k)*SHY control by >=0.05 Sharpe in both windows (K2), none reaches watch_recent, or every apparent pass is beaten by its own same-ticker RAND placebo.
